chief_complaint: swollen lymph node in neck and drenching night sweats
hpi_details: 25M presents with a painless, rubbery lump in his right supraclavicular area for 2 months. Over the last 3 weeks, he has had drenching night sweats requiring him to change his clothes, a low-grade fever, and a 10-pound weight loss.

core_concepts: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and painless lymphadenopathy in a young adult strongly suggest lymphoma.
Diagnosis requires excisional lymph node biopsy showing Reed-Sternberg cells.
common_misconceptions: Assuming it is just reactive lymphadenopathy from a recent cold.
dangerous_errors: Doing a fine needle aspiration (FNA) instead of an excisional biopsy, which often misses the diagnosis.
management_principles: Excisional biopsy, PET-CT for staging, hematology/oncology referral for chemotherapy.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 25M with a painless neck mass, drenching night sweats, and weight loss.
reference_soap.objective: 3cm firm, rubbery, mobile right supraclavicular lymph node. No hepatosplenomegaly.
reference_soap.plan: Excisional lymph node biopsy, CBC, CMP, LDH, refer to hematology.

learning_objectives: Recognize B symptoms and appropriate biopsy technique for lymphoma.

teaching.one_liner: Painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with B symptoms (night sweats, fever, weight loss) in a young adult.

must_ask.say: Is the lump painless, and has it been growing over the past few weeks or months?
Have you had drenching night sweats, fevers, or unexplained weight loss?
Does the swollen area hurt or itch after you drink alcohol?
Did a course of antibiotics from your doctor make any difference to the swelling?
How is your energy level, and has this been affecting your daily activities?

history.answer: I noticed a lump on the lower right side of my neck about two months ago, and lately I have been having severe night sweats.
I first noticed it about two months ago, and it has gradually gotten bigger over time.
It is on the right side of my lower neck, right above my collarbone.
It feels about the size of a walnut or small grape, and it feels like just one firm lump.
I checked my armpits and groin, but I haven't noticed any lumps anywhere else.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I press right on it.
No, it stays right where it is when I swallow or stick out my tongue.
No, eating does not change its size and it does not hurt during meals.
No recent colds, sore throat, toothaches, or skin cuts on my neck or head.
I have been running a low fever and having drenching night sweats for the last three weeks where I have to change my soaked pajamas.
I noticed my clothes feel loose, and when I weighed myself I had lost about ten pounds in the last month without dieting.
No difficulty swallowing, my voice has not changed, and I am not having any trouble breathing.
No earaches, no runny or stuffy nose, no nosebleeds, and no pain when I swallow.
No racing heart, tremors, or trouble tolerating heat or cold.
Actually, a couple of weeks ago I had a beer and noticed an aching pain right in that lump shortly afterward.
A doctor at the campus clinic prescribed me a week of amoxicillin last month thinking it was swollen glands, but it didn't shrink at all.
I have felt much more tired and run down than usual for the past few weeks, making it hard to study.
No, I have never had tuberculosis and I have not been around anyone with chronic cough or TB.
No, I do not have a cat and haven't had any scratches or contact with stray animals.
No, I never received any radiation treatments to my head or neck when I was younger.
I have never had any serious medical conditions or chronic illnesses.
I have never had surgery and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medications or food.
No, I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I drink occasionally with friends on weekends, maybe one or two beers a week.
I am a college student living in a dormitory with a roommate.
I am in a monogamous relationship, and we always use condoms.
No one in my family has had thyroid cancer, lymphoma, or other cancers that I know of.
I was hoping it was just a stubborn lymph node infection that wouldn't go away.
Because it's growing and I'm losing weight and sweating at night, I'm really worried it might be lymphoma or some kind of cancer.
I really want to get a biopsy or whatever test is needed to find out exactly what this lump is.

exam.finding: Young male appears comfortable, mildly fatigued, in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, body temperature 37.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Pharynx is clear without mucosal lesions, tonsillar enlargement, or exudates; dentition is normal.
A 3 cm firm, rubbery, mobile, non-tender lymph node is palpated in the right supraclavicular fossa; no movement on swallowing; no other cervical lymphadenopathy.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, with no palpable nodules; moves normally with deglutition.
Soft, non-tender, non-distended abdomen without guarding or rigidity.
No hepatomegaly or splenomegaly palpable below the costal margins.
